Complete type definitions with field order, offsets, sizes and alignment for fault, virtual CPU, memory management, table page and iterator records.
Ordering, nesting, interrupt context and contention rules for observed locks beyond their hold spans.
Internal methods for frame resolution, huge page tuning, permission evaluation, flush range selection and device entry creation.

findings.text: Provides the main fault entry that builds a fault record from the faulting address and error indications, resolves the guest frame and memory slot for direct roots after clearing host direct bits, then dispatches to the configured handler with a fast path for the common handler under a build option, converts unexpected private emulation requests into a userspace memory fault report, and propagates write to shadow indication and final mapping level to callers.

A new fault record starts with execution, write, present, reservation, user and privacy flags derived from the error value, prefetch and translation type markers supplied by caller context, a maximum huge level cap with request and goal fixed to the smallest page size, and a failure marker for the backing frame until resolution succeeds.
Selects the translation fault worker based on build support and runtime enablement, using the TDP MMU worker when available and otherwise falling back to the legacy direct worker.

The TDP MMU fault flow applies page tracking first, then a fast resolution attempt, then resource preparation and backing frame resolution, and only on continuation enters a shared protected region to discard stale faults, install the mapping, and run final accounting before releasing protection.
The mmu_lock in shared mode is held across staleness validation, table installation and fault finalization, with acquisition after backing frame resolution and release after final accounting.

Implements table installation for a single guest frame by choosing the appropriate root, tuning huge page goals, walking the existing hierarchy, allocating and linking intermediate tables or splitting oversize leaves as needed, recording huge page restrictions, and delegating leaf creation to a dedicated target routine with retry on contention.
Table traversal and leaf installation occur under RCU read side protection, while possible huge page tracking updates are serialized by tdp_mmu_pages_lock.

Leaf handling treats already present permission compatible leaves as spurious, creates a device style entry when no slot exists and a normal entry otherwise, installs it atomically with retry on loss, issues a remote flush when replacement changes mapping shape, and reports write protection versus device emulation versus fixed outcomes.
Root choice depends on whether the fault address is considered direct for the virtual machine, selecting the mirrored root for non direct addresses and the normal root otherwise.

For mirrored shadow pages an additional backing page is reserved from a dedicated per virtual CPU cache for use by the confidential compute module, which performs its own setup while the host uses only its own table pointer.

Write protection handling first rejects repeated faults on the same instruction pointer and address, clears prior retry markers, rejects device cache hits, conditionally attempts unprotect and retry for direct guest table writes or for shadowed cases needing event reinjection, and otherwise requests emulation with retry permission only outside nested guests.
A fault is classified as a write to guest tables only when guest table, write and present indications are all asserted together.

Provides the central instruction emulation service that validates vendor permission, optionally decodes with breakpoint and exception checks, supports skip only completion and vendor backdoor filtering, allows unprotect and retry for non table writing operations, synchronizes register state, executes with nested intercept awareness, and routes exception, port, device and userspace completion outcomes to writeback handling.

Writeback is skipped for inbound port or device reads and pending userspace completions, while otherwise it updates interrupt shadowing, performance counts, instruction pointer, flags and single step handling, and requests event processing when interrupts become enabled.

Emulated exception delivery gives debug vectors to debug injection, page fault vectors to page fault injection with address invalidation on present non reserved faults and separate walks for nested versus normal faults, and other vectors to queued delivery with or without error codes.

Vector classification treats debug as a distinct category requiring extra state, breakpoint and overflow as traps, double fault and machine check as aborts, out of range and non maskable as interrupts, and all remaining including reserved values as faults.

Interrupt shadow updates coalesce repeated identical requests so consecutive operations do not extend shadowing, apply vendor shadow state only on change, and request event processing when shadowing clears.

Frozen or concurrently modified table entries at any walk level force abandonment of allocated tables and a full retry, and faults found stale after acquiring shared protection are discarded without installation.

Unprotect and retry paths carry loop and correctness guards that forbid retry on repeated instruction and address pairs, forbid retry on device cache hits, forbid retry permission inside nested guests, and require unprotect success before skipping emulation.
Externally visible table installation routine callable from other translation units for handling translation faults.
Externally visible instruction emulation entry callable from other virtualization control paths.
Externally visible performance counter hook that records a retired branch for the current virtual CPU.
Externally visible page fault injection helper that validates the vector, selects the appropriate walk, optionally invalidates the cached translation, and delegates to walk specific injection.
Branch retirement accounting forwards to the generic event trigger using the per virtual CPU branch counting set.
Instruction permission checking delegates entirely to the vendor specific validation callback with emulation type and optional instruction bytes.

Observed fault record carries fault address, error value and derived access markers, prefetch and privacy state, translation mode and workaround flags, level limits and goals, backing frame identifier, guest frame number and slot reference, plus outcome markers for writability, huge page restriction and shadow write fault.

Observed management structures include per virtual CPU translation state with direct mode flag and normal plus mirrored roots, per table role with level access and validity markers, per table huge page restriction state and external backing pointer, and per fault iterator state with old entry value level and guest frame.
